skills.name: Atomic number, mass number and nuclide notation

note.text:
Atomic number Z = number of protons (also the number of electrons in a neutral atom). It identifies the element.
Mass number A = number of protons + number of neutrons.
Nuclide notation: the mass number is written at the top left and the atomic number at the bottom left of the symbol, e.g. ²³₁₁Na.
So: protons = Z, electrons = Z (neutral atom), neutrons = A − Z.
Elements are arranged in the Periodic Table in order of atomic number.

sections.heading: Two numbers describe a nucleus
sections.text:
The atomic number Z is the number of protons. It is the identity of the element: {1} proton is hydrogen, {6} is carbon, {8} is oxygen, {11} is sodium.
The mass number A is the total number of protons and neutrons, the heavy particles in the nucleus.
In a neutral atom the number of electrons equals Z.

sections.heading: Nuclide notation
Order in the Periodic Table
sections.text:
The Periodic Table lists the elements in order of increasing atomic number: H ({1}), He ({2}), Li ({3}), … Ca ({20}).
Knowing the first {20} elements and their atomic numbers will help you in every chemistry lesson this year.

key_words.meaning: ᴬ_Z X: A on top, Z below

mistake.why: The top number counts protons and neutrons together.

worked_example.problem: For ²⁷₁₃Al, give the number of protons, neutrons and electrons.

cards.idea: The atomic number identifies the element.
example: Every atom with {6} protons is carbon.

misconceptions.explain: Subtract the atomic number from the mass number.

questions.prompt: In the notation {sup(massNumber(X))}{sub(atomicNumber(X))}{X}, how many protons are there?

misconceptions.explain: The top number is the mass number (protons + neutrons). Protons = the bottom number.

solution: The bottom number is the atomic number = number of protons.

questions.prompt: An atom has {atomicNumber(X)} protons. Which element is it? Give its atomic number.

misconceptions.explain: The number of protons is the atomic number, not the mass number.

solution: The number of protons is the atomic number: {answer}.

misconceptions.explain: Subtract the atomic number from the mass number.

questions.prompt: An atom of {nameOf(X)} has {atomicNumber(X)} protons and {neutrons(X)} neutrons. How is it written in nuclide notation?

misconceptions.explain: The mass number (bigger) goes on top; the atomic number at the bottom.
The top number is protons + neutrons, not neutrons alone.
The mass number is protons + neutrons = {massNumber(X)}.

questions.prompt: An atom has {e} electrons and {n} neutrons. What is its mass number?

misconceptions.explain: Electrons do not count in the mass number: A = protons + neutrons.
